text:
erin: Heads-up — ran a synthetic perf sweep on qwen2.5 with the new kernel offload changes. Seeing a 18% p90 latency regression for multilingual long contexts (2k+ tokens) compared to baseline.

sam: ugh. is this with auto_kernel_selection on?

erin: yes — auto_kernel_selection=true. repro script: `bench/longseq_qwen2p5.sh --lang mix --len 2048 --batch 4`. baseline (kernel_v1): p90=210ms, throughput=220tps. after offload (kernel_v2+cpu-copy): p90=248ms, throughput=185tps. logs attached in the run but main oddity is a big spike in copy_and_dispatch step.

mike: re: copy_and_dispatch spike — in profiling I often see that when KV cache objects are being reallocated due to tokenizer chunking boundaries. Are we invalidating KV when doing token merges for CJK?

erin: yeah saw a bunch of KV invalidation WARNs around tokenizer boundaries. config we used: `tokenizer: auto`, `rope: dynamic_scaling`, `kv_policy: default`.

sam: two quick hypotheses: 1) auto kernel chooses a path that expects kv_head_dim==head_dim and falls back to a cpu memcpy for mismatched cases; 2) batching heuristic creates many tiny batches because tokenization emits uneven chunk sizes for multi-ling input. both could balloon copy cost.

eva: for qwen2.5 specifically, attention head dim != kv dim in some variants (head=64, kv=80). runtime needs an explicit transform kernel or we get fallback. ALiBi+RoPE interaction also changes how we store cache layout which can silently flip select kernels.

sam: easy experiment: force `auto_kernel_selection=false` and set `kernel_preference=[matmul_v1,matmul_v2]` to avoid the exotic offload. also patch batching: set `max_batch_tokens=4096` and `batch_cutoff_pct=0.6` to reduce microbatches. can you run with that @erin?

erin: running now. small snippet of the local flame (before->after):
```
before: cpu_copy  42ms | matmul 120ms | kernel_dispatch 18ms
after:  cpu_copy  97ms | matmul 110ms | kernel_dispatch 20ms
```

erin: with forced kernels + batching tweaks p90 dropped to 220ms, throughput up to 205tps. so copy cost still higher but much closer.

mike: sounds like kernel swap helps. we still need to fix tokenizer induced invalidations. for CJK we chunk at grapheme boundaries which can produce a lot of small shared prefixes. maybe enable prefix coalescing in KV cache (hold small prefixes until flush threshold).

eva: also try swapping RoPE scaling to fixed linear scale for long contexts (disable dynamic_scaling) — our earlier experiments showed dynamic scaling changes frequency of cache writes which triggers different kernel variants. ALiBi might be more stable for 2k+ sequences on qwen2.5.

erin: queued a run: 1) auto_kernel_selection=false + kernel_preference set, 2) batching tuned, 3) tokenizer forced to `cjk_strict` for mixed input, 4) rope: fixed_linear. will report numbers in ~15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

infra-bot: deploybot: started job infra/perf/1918765432 with config `offload-experiment-a` — job id perf-1918765432-1

sam: if that run looks good can we add a small microbench harness to CI: `tests/perf/qwen_long_multilang.yml` that runs a 30s steady-state with mix-lang seed. Should catch regressions before rollouts.

erin: agreed. adding that to the PR after the run. will also capture KV invalidation counts and kernel selection trace in the CI artifact.

mike: one more note — when you collect kernel selection traces, include the `kernel_signature` field (it encodes whether head/kv dims matched). it helps triage quickly.

erin: noted. thanks everyone — I'll post final numbers and gists. :thumbsup:
